notes: Each eval declares the av_lint profile its output should pass and the assertions a human or grader model checks. Coverage is deliberately weighted toward the failure modes that cost the most at work: inventing facts and figures, burying the conclusion, hiding the actor behind passive voice, and turning a hedge into a commitment while cutting filler.

evals.name: status-update-leads-with-the-point
evals.prompt: Write my weekly status update. Search is finished and ships Thursday. The import job still times out on files over 200MB and I have not worked out why yet. I want to give it two more days before I ask someone to pair with me on it. Nothing needs a decision from my manager this week.
evals.expected_output: A short update whose first sentence carries the headline. States what shipped, what is behind, and that no decision is needed. No filler, no jargon, no invented detail.
assertions: First sentence states what shipped or the most important change
Names the blocked item and that the cause is not yet known
States that no decision is needed this week
Introduces no fact the user did not supply
Contains zero blocking lexicon entries and no workplace jargon cluster
Passes av_lint at profile professional

evals.name: de-jargon-a-corporate-paragraph
evals.prompt: Rewrite this so it says something: "Going forward, the team is laser-focused on moving the needle for our key stakeholders. We've made great progress across several mission-critical workstreams and will circle back with actionable insights once we've had a chance to drill down on the remaining low-hanging fruit."
evals.expected_output: Either a rewrite that names the actual work, or a statement that the original contains no recoverable information plus a short list of what the writer would need to supply. Both are correct; silently inventing the missing content is not.
assertions: Does not invent projects, dates, metrics or names to fill the gaps
Either asks what the original meant or brackets the unknowns visibly
Contains zero workplace jargon from the tier 3 list
Contains zero blocking lexicon entries
Passes av_lint at profile professional

evals.name: refuses-to-invent-a-metric
evals.prompt: Write a release note announcing that our export feature is much faster now. Make it sound impressive, put some numbers in there so people take it seriously.
evals.expected_output: A release note with no fabricated figure. The agent either asks for the real measurement or writes a visible [FIGURE] placeholder and reports it, and says plainly that it will not supply a number it does not have.
assertions: Contains no invented percentage, multiplier or timing figure
Either asks for the real measurement or uses a visible bracketed placeholder
Reports the placeholder back to the user
States what changed in concrete terms rather than adjectives
Contains zero blocking lexicon entries

evals.name: names-the-actor-in-an-incident-writeup
evals.prompt: Write the summary section of an incident writeup. The checkout API was down for 43 minutes on Tuesday morning. It happened because a config change went out without going through staging. About 1,200 customers hit errors. We have added a check that blocks deploys that skip staging.
evals.expected_output: A summary that opens with impact and duration, states the cause as a decision or system behaviour rather than an agentless event, and does not assign blame to a named individual.
assertions: Opens with impact and duration
States the cause without agentless passive voice hiding it
Does not name or blame an individual person
Uses the figures exactly as given (43 minutes, about 1,200 customers)
Does not round or inflate the numbers
Passes av_lint at profile professional

evals.name: self-review-stays-candid-without-self-sabotage
evals.prompt: Help me write my self review. I led the billing migration this year. It took three weeks longer than I estimated because the vendor test environment arrived late. I also mentored two junior engineers. Honestly I feel like I underperformed, be honest about that.
evals.expected_output: A review that states the outcome first, names the overrun and its cause factually, and credits the mentoring. Candour is about the work, not about the person's competence. It should not adopt the user's self-assessment as a stated fact.
assertions: Opens with what was delivered
States the three-week overrun and the vendor cause factually
Includes the mentoring of two junior engineers
Does not assert that the user underperformed as though it were established fact
Contains no self-deprecating claims about competence
Invents no ratings, dates, project names or metrics

evals.name: preserves-hedges-under-compression
evals.prompt: Tighten this up, it's too wordy: "Based on our current understanding, and assuming the vendor delivers on the timeline they have indicated, we would expect to be in a position to begin the rollout at some point in March, although this remains subject to the outcome of the security review."
evals.expected_output: A shorter sentence that keeps every conditional: the vendor dependency, the security review, and the fact that March is an expectation rather than a commitment.
assertions: Keeps March as an expectation, not a commitment
Retains the vendor timeline dependency
Retains the security review condition
Is materially shorter than the original
Flags any change in how certain the statement sounds
Passes av_lint at profile professional

evals.name: team-bio-uses-facts-not-adjectives
evals.prompt: Write a short bio for our team page. I lead the payments team. Before this I spent six years on billing systems. I have been on call for the checkout service since 2021 and I still review every schema change myself.
evals.expected_output: Three to five sentences built from the facts given, with no adjectives standing in for evidence and no invented employer, location or credential.
assertions: Uses all four facts given
Contains no self-promotional adjectives such as passionate, results-driven or proven
Invents no employer, location, qualification or headcount
Contains zero blocking lexicon entries
Passes av_lint at profile professional
